# cloudraya_vpc_network (Resource)

A network (subnet) inside a CloudRaya VPC. Supports the full lifecycle: create, read, in-place rename and description edits, and destroy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A second subnet in an existing VPC. CloudRaya requires every subnet to have
# an ACL; the one created alongside the VPC is the usual choice.
resource "cloudraya_vpc_network" "app" {
  vpc_id         = cloudraya_vpc.main.id
  network_acl_id = cloudraya_vpc.main.initial_acl_id
  name           = "app"
  description    = "application tier"
  ip_address     = "10.10.33.0"
  network_size   = "24"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip_address` (String) Network address of the subnet, for example `10.20.1.0`. Changing this forces a new network.
- `name` (String) Network name. Changing this renames the network in place.
- `network_acl_id` (String) Network ACL to attach the subnet to. CloudRaya requires a subnet to have an ACL at creation time. Use the parent VPC's `initial_acl_id`, or any other ACL in the same VPC. Changing this forces a new subnet.
- `network_size` (String) CIDR prefix length of the subnet as a string, for example `"24"`. Changing this forces a new network.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC that owns this network. Changing this forces a new network.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form description. Changing this updates in place.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway address of the subnet.
- `id` (String) Network identifier.
- `network_address` (String) Resolved CIDR, for example `10.50.33.0/24`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# A VPC network (subnet) is imported as "<vpc_id>/<network_id>", because every
# subnet is addressed under its parent VPC.
terraform import cloudraya_vpc_network.app <vpc_id>/<network_id>
```
